To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
iNOS expression in human glial cells is restricted to astrocytic cells.
inducible nitric oxide (iNOS, also called NOS2) expression is selectively induced only in astrocytes derived from human fetal or adult brains.
iNOS expression was induced in cultures of astrocyte-enriched cells isolated from adult human brains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of nitric oxide (NO) in the brain.
the role of astrocytes in the inflammatory response.
elucidating the mechanisms of iNOS induction and regulation in human astrocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
iNOS expression in astrocytes, as in microglia and neurons, can be induced by cytokines, and is regulated by species, cell type, and age of the cells.
iNOS is selectively induced in human astrocytes, regardless of the age of the tissue donor.
iNOS is selectively induced in adult human astrocyte cultures, whereas microglia do not express iNOS in either fetal or adult human brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
iNOS expression in astrocytes is a characteristic of human astrocytes and that iNOS is not induced by cytokines in adult human microglia.
in both human fetal and adult astrocytes, iNOS expression is inducible, and is regulated in a similar manner.
the iNOS gene expression is regulated in a similar fashion in human fetal and adult astrocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of iNos in astrocytes can be induced by a combination of cytokines in adult human brain, and this is an important finding because iNos is a critical enzyme in the production of nitric oxide (NO) which is known to be neurotoxic.
the induction of iNOS in astrocytes is not restricted to fetal astrocytes, and thus the role of astrocytic iNOS in human diseases such as stroke may be similar to that in other species.
the ability to produce iNOS in astrocytes is conserved across species and is present in both fetal and adult astrocytes.
